newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil trundles behind crude, market quieter.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil trundles behind crude, market quieter.

text.p: Fuel oil trundled behind soaring crude futures that easily passed $24 a barrel before profit-taking. Activity was slow after Wednesday's business.

High sulphur cracked barges surpassed Wednesday's prices with a trade done at $118 fob ARA and several at $117. Levels eased slightly but the mood was firm on the back of the continued concern about Iraq, tightish supplies and an increase in barge buyers who expect further rises.
High sulphur cargoes were also stronger, backing coming from a deal yesterday at $108 fob NWE into the U.K. and unconfirmed talk that 25kt was concluded today at between mean cif and cif

high NWE. A slight backwardation into October was inhibiting remaining buying interest and the market looks better balanced than a week ago. "There is not much product out there, but also not many interest for September," said one trader.

Low sulphur were also perkier. Sellers were only talking floating prices, hoping the contango into October materialises. Sellers with flexibility to hold cargo were expecting to roll barrels into October. Interest for September barrels was lacking. A low sulphur lot of 8,000 tonnes was sold into the UK at high fob +$1 loading September 17-19. There was unconfirmed talk that a Gravenchon cargo was done, possibly for Portugal.
